plain.li: Up for the first time in days. I made it to the door and back and had to sit down.
Weak as a newborn foal. They say it passes in a week or two.
My legs have forgotten what they're for. Walked to the table for supper anyway.
[bed] So many days in bed that the floor feels strange under my feet.
[bed] I could draw the ceiling over that bed from memory. I'm glad to be looking at a different one.
[bed,winter] Out of bed at last, and it's winter out there. Even the cold air smells good.
[limb] I keep reaching with the hand that isn't there. Then I remember.
[limb] Learning to do everything a new way. Buttons are the worst.
[limb] I lost part of myself out there. The rest of me is still here, and it's tired.
[surgery] {OTHER_nameDef} says the operation went well. I'll believe it when I can stand up without seeing stars.
[surgery] Woke up stitched and sore. {OTHER_nameDef} was sitting by the bed, looking more tired than I felt.
[surgery,!lowtech] The anesthetic has worn off and I wish it hadn't. {OTHER_nameDef} says the soreness means it's healing.
[surgery,lowtech] {OTHER_nameDef} gave me something bitter to drink before the knife and something sweeter after. I remember neither.
[illness] The fever's gone. What it left behind is a body that tires walking across a room.
[illness] Ate a whole bowl of stew today. Then slept for four hours.
[illness,old] At my age, getting over a thing like that takes its time. I'll take the time.
[child] I was really sick and now I'm better, but I still have to rest. Resting is boring.

warm.li: Everyone keeps asking how I'm doing. I'm doing well enough to be embarrassed by it.
[surgery] I owe {OTHER_nameDef} more than I can say. I'll start with a thank-you and work up.

cheerful.li: Still standing! Mostly sitting, but still.
[patient] Doctor's orders are to rest and eat. I can follow orders.

gloomy.li: Survived. That's what they keep telling me, as if I'd argue.
[limb] They saved the rest of me. I'm still deciding how I feel about that.

cold.li: Recovery period. Expected to last a week or two. Reduced work in the meantime.
[impatient] I can do half my work at half speed. That's better than none, whatever they say.

plain.li: Went back to work too soon. By midday I was sitting in the dirt, shaking. More days of rest, they say.
I thought I was ready. My body disagreed, loudly, in front of the others.
Overdid it. Back to taking it slow.
[impatient] I only meant to carry one load. One turned into the whole afternoon, and now I'm paying for it.
[impatient] The doctor said a week. I gave it four days. Now it's going to be longer than a week.
[winter] Carried firewood before I should have. My arms gave out halfway to the stove.

warm.li: Someone found me sitting by the path and walked me home without a word of told-you-so. I'll rest now.

cheerful.li: Lesson learned: rest first, heroics later.

gloomy.li: Every time I think I'm better, I'm not.

cold.li: Returned to work prematurely. Recovery extended by a few days.

plain.li: Carried a full load today and didn't need to stop. I'm myself again.
Slept through the night and woke up hungry. That's the end of being an invalid.
Worked a whole day and only felt the ordinary kind of tired.
Ran the last stretch home today, just to see if I could. I could.
[old] Back to my old self, aches and all. The usual aches, at least.
[child] I'm better now. I'm allowed to run again.

warm.li: Strong enough to help again. I've a lot of favors to pay back.

cheerful.li: Good as new, or close enough!

plain.li: Company today. {OTHER_nameDef} came by, and we talked about the harvest and who's feuding with whom.
{OTHER_nameDef} pulled up a chair and stayed most of the afternoon. I hadn't realized how long the days in bed had been.
The news, a cup of something hot and a bad joke, all from {OTHER_nameDef}. All three helped.
Fell asleep while {OTHER_nameDef} was reading to me. I'll have to ask how it ended.
[convalescing] Less like a ghost today, says {OTHER_nameDef}. High praise.
[winter] {OTHER_nameDef} came in stamping snow off {OTHER_possessive} boots and stayed until the candle burned down.
[child] {OTHER_nameDef} came to see me and told me a story. It was a good one.

warm.li: I'm lucky in my friends. {OTHER_nameDef} sat with me half the day.

cheerful.li: {OTHER_nameDef} did impressions of the whole council until my sides hurt.

gloomy.li: It's easier being ill with someone in the chair by the bed. Today it was {OTHER_nameDef}.

plain.li: [patient] {OTHER_nameDef} tended me today. I'd trust no one else with a knife.
[patient] When {OTHER_nameDef} says it'll mend, it mends. I've stopped worrying.
[patient] {OTHER_nameDef} looked at the wound, nodded once and got to work. I relaxed the moment I saw that nod.
[patient,renowned] I've lost count of the people {OTHER_nameDef} has patched up. Now I'm one more.
[surgery] {OTHER_nameDef} opened me up and put me back together. I keep looking at the scar. It's very neat.
[surgery,first] I was frightened of the operation. {OTHER_nameDef} explained every step and then did exactly that.
[surgery,trusted] The others told me I'd be fine with {OTHER_nameDef} doing it. They were right, and I've stopped shaking.
[word] If I'm ever badly hurt, I want {OTHER_nameDef}, and I've told the others so.
[word] {OTHER_nameDef} has steady hands and a steadier head. I've seen both at work.
[word,renowned] People here say "{OTHER_nameDef} will see to it" the way others say "it'll be fine".
[word,lowtech] The old ones say {OTHER_nameDef} has a healer's hands. I believe them.

warm.li: [patient] {OTHER_nameDef} sat with me after tending me, just to make sure. I felt looked after.
[word] I'm grateful we have {OTHER_nameDef}. I don't say it enough.

cheerful.li: [patient] With {OTHER_nameDef} on it, I'll be up in no time!

gloomy.li: [word] Out here, you'd better have a good doctor. We do. {OTHER_nameDef}.

cold.li: [word] {OTHER_nameDef}'s results speak for themselves. I'd choose {OTHER_objective}.

plain.li: Operated on {OTHER_nameDef} today. It went the way it was supposed to, which is the best thing you can say about an operation.
Finished with {OTHER_nameDef} by lamplight. My hands didn't start shaking until it was over.
{OTHER_nameDef} came through the operation. I stood at the basin washing my hands long after they were clean.
Three hours on {OTHER_nameDef}. Every stitch where it should be.
[brain] Operated inside {OTHER_nameDef}'s skull today. I didn't breathe properly until {OTHER_pronoun} woke and said my name.
[lowtech] A sharp knife, boiled cloths and a steady hand. {OTHER_nameDef} will mend.

warm.li: {OTHER_nameDef} squeezed my hand before going under. I'm glad I could give {OTHER_objective} good news when {OTHER_pronoun} woke.

cheerful.li: {OTHER_nameDef}'s operation went perfectly. I'd like more days like this one.

gloomy.li: {OTHER_nameDef} lived through the knife. Not everyone does.

plain.li: [trusted] People have started coming to me first when something's wrong. I didn't ask for that, but I'll try to deserve it.
[trusted] Someone called me "the doctor" today, not "the one who does the bandages". I answered to it before I noticed.
[trusted] Wrote down everyone I've pulled through so far. It's a longer list than I thought.
[renowned] They trust me with their lives now, every one of them. Some nights that's a heavy thing to carry.
[renowned] I've kept more people alive than I can easily count. I still remember each of the ones I couldn't.

warm.li: [trusted] People thank me in the dining hall now. I never know where to look.

blunt.li: They trust me. Fine. I'll keep doing the work.

cheerful.li: [trusted] Apparently I'm good at this! Who knew.

gloomy.li: The more they trust me, the worse it'll be when I fail one of them.

cold.li: My results have been noticed. Good. Trust makes patients easier.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} died today, and the last one is barely in the ground. I don't know what I'm doing wrong.
Lost {OTHER_nameDef}. That's two in a few days. I sat in the infirmary after and couldn't make myself clean up.
Everyone keeps telling me it isn't my fault. They're very careful about how they say it.
[surgery] {OTHER_nameDef} didn't wake up from the operation. I keep seeing my own hands.
[lowtech] The old healers said every healer has a dark season. I think this is mine.

warm.li: I washed {OTHER_nameDef} and dressed {OTHER_objective} myself. It's the last thing I could do.

blunt.li: Another one dead. {OTHER_nameDef}. I need to sleep.

cheerful.li: I can't find anything bright to write today. {OTHER_nameDef} is gone.

gloomy.li: {OTHER_nameDef} too. Maybe someone else should hold the knife.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} died in my care. Two losses in a short time. I'll review my methods.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} died on the table. I did everything right, I think. I'll be thinking about it for a long time.
The operation on {OTHER_nameDef} went wrong, and then it went worse. I couldn't bring {OTHER_objective} back.
{OTHER_nameDef} trusted me to do it. I keep coming back to that.

warm.li: I talked to {OTHER_nameDef} the whole time, even after. I hope some of it was heard.

cheerful.li: I'll remember {OTHER_nameDef} joking before the operation. That's what I'll keep.

gloomy.li: {OTHER_nameDef} died because I opened {OTHER_objective} up. However I put it, that's what happened.

cold.li: Fatal complication during {OTHER_nameDef}'s operation. The risk was known.

plain.li: Delivered {OTHER_nameDef}'s baby today. {BABY_nameDef} came out red-faced and furious, which is exactly how it should be.
{BABY_nameDef} was born in the small hours. {OTHER_nameDef} did the hard part; I mostly caught.
Long labor, but {OTHER_nameDef} and the baby are both fine. {BABY_nameDef}. Good name.
Washed {BABY_nameDef}, wrapped {BABY_objective} and handed {BABY_objective} to {OTHER_nameDef}. Then I sat down. Nine hours on my feet.
[first] My first birth. I read everything I could find beforehand and still felt like I knew nothing. {BABY_nameDef} didn't seem to mind.
[first] Brought a child into the world today. My hands are still shaking, in a good way.
[winter] {BABY_nameDef} was born on a cold night, with the stove roaring and every blanket we have.
[lowtech] Boiled water, clean cloths and a lot of waiting. Then {BABY_nameDef}, all at once.

warm.li: Held {BABY_nameDef} before anyone else did. I'll never get tired of that.

cheerful.li: We have a new colonist, and {BABY_pronoun} has opinions already!

gloomy.li: {BABY_nameDef} is here, safe for now. I hope this place is kind to {BABY_objective}.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef} delivered my baby. I don't remember most of it, except {OTHER_possessive} voice telling me what to do next.
I was terrified, and {OTHER_nameDef} wasn't. That helped more than anything.
{OTHER_nameDef} stayed with me the whole night. I'll never forget that.
[experienced] {OTHER_nameDef} has done this before, many times. I could tell from the first minute.

warm.li: My child came into the world in {OTHER_nameDef}'s hands. I'll make sure the child knows it, one day.

blunt.li: {OTHER_nameDef} delivered the baby. Did it well.

cheerful.li: {OTHER_nameDef} was wonderful. My baby is wonderful. Everything is wonderful and I need to sleep.

gloomy.li: It could have gone badly. With {OTHER_nameDef} there, it didn't.

cold.li: {OTHER_nameDef} handled the delivery competently. I'll remember that.

plain.li: {OTHER_nameDef}'s baby never breathed. I did everything I know. I sat with {OTHER_objective} afterward, because there was nothing else to do.
A still birth today. I keep my voice steady in the room and lose it outside.
I wrapped the child and put it in {OTHER_nameDef}'s arms. There are no words for that, so I didn't try any.

warm.li: I stayed with {OTHER_nameDef} until morning. It's all I could give.

blunt.li: The baby didn't live. Nothing to be done.

gloomy.li: Some births end like this. Knowing that doesn't help.

cold.li: Stillbirth. {OTHER_nameDef} will need watching for a while.
